messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: auth provider (Okta) is returning intermittent 502 / 5xx for token verification endpoints. Multiple downstream systems reporting failed logins and console session checks. Paging SRE rotation. /cc @Samir (SRE) :rotating_light:

Samir (SRE): ack. seeing 502s from https://login.okta.com/oauth2/v1/introspect and /v1/keys in the logs. A bunch of token verification calls failing with 502 -> we currently treat as transient but rates are high.

Jordan (Support): customer facing: several accounts reporting login failures (web + mobile). Support tickets #4521, #4522, #4523. Early customers impacted: acme-corp (prod), beta-shop (staging->prod). Need ETA for mitigation to send to customers.

Maya (Product): service impact: console sessions failing for some customers, especially when reauth is required. We need to know scope (percent of auth requests failing) and if any sessions are being invalidated erroneously.

Samir (SRE): quick summary from logs: spike of 5xx started ~10m ago, error rate ~13% of verify-token calls across regions N. Cache miss rate for JWKS also up (timeouts against Okta keys endpoint). Hypothesis: Okta service degradation causing upstream 5xx -> token verify path fails.

Eli (Infra): can we flip to cached JWKS and local validation to avoid hitting Okta for each call? We have a fallback path but it's off for a subset of routes. Recommend enabling local-jwks-fallback for auth-proxy.

Sachin (DevEx): we have a small script to prime the local JWKS cache and validate tokens offline. dropping it here:```bash
# prime JWKS from last-known good endpoint
curl -sS https://okta.example.com/oauth2/v1/keys -o /tmp/okta-keys.json
# restart auth-proxy with LOCAL_JWKS=/tmp/okta-keys.json
sudo systemctl restart redwood-auth-proxy
```
Use with caution, keys might be stale for rotated keys.

Samir (SRE): executing canary: enabling local-jwks-fallback on auth-proxy in us-east-1 only, 10% rollout to start. If successful, ramp to 100% and then other regions.

oncall-bot: deploy job started: auth-proxy/local-jwks-fallback -> canary (us-east-1, 10%)

Samir (SRE): canary metrics after 3m: verify error rate in canary dropped from 12% -> 1.5%. CPU latency unchanged. Good sign.

Jordan (Support): update for customers: "We're seeing a degradation in a third-party auth provider impacting logins. We're applying a safe fallback to reduce failed logins; you'll see improvement in the next few minutes. We'll follow up with a full incident summary." Sending to acme-corp and beta-shop now.

Maya (Product): please capture the rollback plan if fallback fails. We need clear comms and a timeline for when we declare full mitigation.

Samir (SRE): rollback: remove local-jwks-fallback and re-route to primary Okta endpoint. Also can disable auth-proxy change via feature-flag quickly.

Eli (Infra): reaching out to Okta support via enterprise channel. Okta Status shows partial outage in login services: https://status.okta.com/incidents/xyz (Okta Status Bot attached).

Okta Status Bot: Official: "We are investigating increased 502/5xx for token introspection and key service. Our engineers are working on mitigation." (link: https://status.okta.com/incidents/xyz)

Samir (SRE): ramp plan: if canary holds for 10m with error rate <2%, promote to 100% in region and then replicate to eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. Monitor reauth flows and console login metrics.

Sachin (DevEx): also enabling request-level retries with exponential backoff for token-verification calls (2 retries, jitter). Patch diff:```json
{"retries":2, "backoff":"exponential", "jitter":true}```
This should reduce transient failures when Okta recovers.

Samir (SRE): promoted to 100% us-east-1 at +12m. Observed global auth failure rate drop from 13% -> 3% across fleet. Console sessions success rate up.

Jordan (Support): updating support tickets: customers reporting improvement. Will keep them posted when we finish regional rollouts.

Maya (Product): classify incident severity? Currently customer-visible degraded login experience grouped under P1 (partial outage) until resolved.

Samir (SRE): agreed. Opening incident page and timeline. I'll collect logs, svcs, and request counts for postmortem.

Eli (Infra): rolling the fallback to EU and APAC. Please coordinate with oncall in those regions for any local quirks.

Samir (SRE): note: watch for key rotation edgecases: if Okta rotated keys recently, our cached keys could fail for tokens issued after rotation. That's why we limited rollout and included retries.

oncall-bot: incident update: local-jwks-fallback rollout complete in all regions. Error rate down to 1.2%. monitoring for 30m.

Jordan (Support): customers notified. No escalations to C-suite yet. Preparing post-incident customer summary.

Maya (Product): next steps: postmortem with timeline, root cause (third-party degradation), mitigation timeline, recommendations (supporting local fallback, circuit breaker and more robust jwks caching), and communications artifact.

Samir (SRE): handing off to next oncall: @Eli you're the rotation lead for next 2h, please keep monitoring and own postmortem collection. Leaving notes in the incident doc.

Eli (Infra): taking handoff. I'll also open ticket with Okta asking for request logs around our tenant for the 20m window.

oncall-bot: page cleared for on-call rotation handoff. Reminder: add follow-up tasks: postmortem, customer summary, infra change to make fallback automatic when third-party 5xx spike detected.

Jordan (Support): adding follow-up tasks to support board and marking affected customers for outreach in next 24h.

Samir (SRE): TL;DR: Okta degraded -> our token verification calls failed; we enabled local JWKS fallback + retries -> reduced failures significantly; rolling to all regions; handoff to Eli for follow-up and postmortem.

Eli (Infra): will coordinate postmortem and close incident after 24h monitoring.

Jordan (Support): thanks team :thumbsup:

Samir (SRE): closing the on-call view for now, will re-open if Okta status changes.

oncall-bot: Incident state: monitoring. Incident severity: P1 (degraded). Assigned: Eli (Infra).
